tasks.title: A declined action says so — the producer for "nothing happened, and here is why"
tasks.description:
An action that runs but **declines** currently vanishes. From a keypress that is tolerable; from the command palette, where the user deliberately picked the entry out of a list, it reads as a broken command.

## The report that produced this task (2026-07-30)

The maintainer chose **Move Column Up** in the palette and nothing happened. The action is not dead: `handle_move_column_up` (`heca/src/handlers.rs:356`) moves the active column **to the workspace above** and returns early when `current_ws == 0`; `handle_move_column_down` :370 does the same at the last workspace. Correct behaviour, invisible outcome.

It is not one action. The same silent early return is everywhere a precondition can fail:
- no workspace above/below (`move_column_up` / `move_column_down`, `move_pane_*`),
- nothing under the cursor (a component's `perform` returns `Handled::No` — `heca/src/providers/mod.rs` documents "a silent decline is a real answer, not an error"),
- no link under the caret (`open_link_at_caret`), no selection (`copy_selection`), no scrollback to page through,
- a component action whose owner is not mounted (`IntentOutcome::NotRunnable`), one the domain refuses (`IntentOutcome::Blocked`), and one called without its required arguments (`IntentOutcome::MissingArgs`, added F003/P085/T358) — those three are already **named outcomes** on the dispatch path and today only reach a `#[cfg(debug_assertions)] eprintln!`.

## What to build here

A notification producer on the dispatch path: when an intent resolves to `Blocked`, `NotRunnable` or `MissingArgs`, or a handler declines, raise a low-severity notification saying which action and why. `dispatch_view_intent` (`heca/src/app/interaction.rs`) already computes exactly those outcomes and throws them away for every caller but RPC — that is the seam, and it needs no new plumbing.

The gap to close is the **handler** case: an early `return` inside `handle_move_column_up` is invisible to the dispatcher. Either handlers gain a way to report a decline (a return value, or a `cx`-style sink), or the well-known preconditions are checked before dispatch. That choice is this task's real content — do not paper over it by special-casing the two column actions.

## The related, deliberately separate question

**Prevention, not just reporting**: an optional `can_perform(&self, id) -> bool` would let the palette render an entry *disabled* rather than let it be chosen and then decline. `DropdownItem` already carries an `enabled` flag, so the menu half exists. That was deferred in F003/P085/T358 ("Do not build it now") and belongs with the palette work, not here — this task is about telling the user what happened, not about greying entries out.

## Behaviors to preserve

A decline is **not an error** and must not read as one: severity low, no modal, no sound. Silence stays correct for a keypress that repeats (holding `j` at the end of a list must not spray toasts) — rate-limit or suppress repeats of the same action, which is the store's job (`notification-02`), not a special case here.

tasks.title: Add name-keyed `notify` action — the raise capability
tasks.description:
Raising a notification today is `state.notifications.push(NotificationDraft, now)` (heca/src/notification.rs, ported from origin/feature/notification-system@ceade1e) — a private Rust method on AppState's store. No plugin, RPC caller, or keybinding can reach it; only dismiss (NotificationDismissOne/All/Last, P059) is a real registered action. This closes that asymmetry.

What exists to build on: `register_dynamic(registry, catalog, meta, handler)` at heca/src/actions.rs:418, `unregister_dynamic` at heca/src/actions.rs:471 — the name-keyed action path documented in docs/widgets.md:4863 "Registering a custom (name-keyed) action". AGENTS.md:1554 "Adding New Actions", the paragraph after step 11: a name-keyed action skips steps 1-4/8 (no WmAction variant, no action_from_name/build_action/priority/ActionRegistry::ALL descriptor).

Register `notify` via register_dynamic — NOT a WmAction variant. A future WASM plugin can only ever dispatch by name, never add an enum variant, and "any plugin can raise a notification" is the point of this action.

Declared args (ArgSpec, pattern at docs/widgets.md:4897):
- title: Text, required
- body: Text, optional
- severity: Enum (info|success|warning|danger), optional, default info
- dedup_key: Text, optional

Handler builds a NotificationDraft from the args (NotificationDraft::new(title).body(..).severity(..).dedup_key(..)) and calls state.notifications.push(draft, Instant::now()).

No action-button argument in v1 — deliberate scope, not a widget limitation: ToastSpec/ToastAction already support several typed actions per card (T487, landed on heca-4b's side), but there is no ArgKind for a nested Intent, so an RPC caller or a keybinding has no typed way to say "and run this other action with these args" as one argument value. A Rust-internal caller that wants a button uses NotificationDraft::action(label, intent) directly with a real Intent it already holds — unaffected by this task.

ActionPolicy: Global (app-level, no layout impact, must keep working while a floating pane is up) — cross-check against T213.

Edge cases: wire RPC parser support in heca/src/rpc.rs same as any other action; a default keybinding is optional (raising a static notification via keybinding is an unusual use case — command palette + RPC are the primary doors).

---

SHIPPED: register_notify_action(registry, catalog) in heca/src/notification.rs, called once from HecaApp::resumed() in main.rs (after providers::register_provider_actions). Registered via register_dynamic — no WmAction variant. Args: title(Text,required)/body(Text,optional)/severity(Enum,optional,default info)/dedup_key(Text,optional). Handler builds a NotificationDraft and calls state.notifications.push. ActionPolicy::Global. Added NotificationSeverity: EnumArg+FromStr (accepts info/success/warning/danger/error) for the severity arg's declared vocabulary. CORRECTION to this task's own "edge cases" text: no rpc.rs changes needed — confirmed the generic `action <name> key=val` RPC verb (heca/src/rpc.rs parse_rpc) already reaches any declared action generically, built-in or name-keyed, with zero per-action code. No default keybinding, by design (command palette + RPC are the doors). VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean. NOT verified: never actually invoked yet (no running app).
